03 — Projects

Selected work

Jarvis — Smart Job Interview Platform Using LLM
Graduation Project

An AI-powered mock interview platform simulating real interviews across Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, and AI/Data Science domains.

  • Integrated four core components: Whisper-based speech-to-text, an 11-feature acoustic emotion detection engine, an NLP semantic scoring engine (cosine similarity), and automated feedback generation.
  • Designed a weighted scoring system — 65% semantic similarity, 35% emotion — delivered through a FastAPI + WebSocket interface.
  • Validated across 6 test sessions with consistent score separation between high‑ and low‑performance interviews.

Deepfake Detection System (CNN‑LSTM)
93.87% val. accuracy

A hybrid CNN‑LSTM model for detecting deepfake videos, pairing EfficientNet‑B0 for spatial feature extraction with LSTM for temporal analysis.

  • Built a hybrid training set from FaceForensics++ and DFD — 192,000+ frames — with an MTCNN-based face extraction and preprocessing pipeline.
  • Shipped a web app for video upload and real-time authenticity prediction.

Research

Supervised Learning Methods: A Systematic Review
1000+ articles reviewed

A solo-authored systematic review surveying supervised learning methods in Machine Learning published between 2022–2024, drawing on IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and ScienceDirect.

  • Reviewed classification, regression, ensemble, and deep learning approaches — including Decision Trees, SVM, ANN, Random Forest, CNN, LSTM, and Transformer-based LLMs.
  • Mapped real-world applications across healthcare, finance, image recognition, and NLP.

The Effect of AI Personal Assistants on Human Decision‑Making Confidence
r = 0.33 trust–confidence correlation

A quantitative, survey-based study examining how AI personal assistants — like Siri, Alexa, and Google Assistant — affect users' confidence in everyday and complex decision-making.

  • Ran a cross-sectional survey with a 10-item, 5-point Likert questionnaire and tested three hypotheses using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation.
  • Found AI assistants positively influence day-to-day decision confidence, and are moderately useful for complex decisions like healthcare or finance.
  • Found a moderate positive correlation (r = 0.33) between trust in AI assistants and decision-making confidence.
